title: Been building an RTS and I don't know if it's a waste of time
author: Crignog
selftext: Title really - I've been building this RTS game for a couple of weeks and I'm at a stage where I'm questioning if I'm wasting my time with it. Does anyone want to try playing it? Feels like scope is probably too high and there isn't really a reason for someone to play it instead of another fully established game.

comments.author: Gurkage
comments.body: It's not for me, but are you having fun? I've built loads of games that didn't make the cut, but I had a lot of fun. Time well spent I'd say.

replies.author: Crignog
replies.body: It's a good point - seeing stuff come together has been a blast. I think I might just be at a point where I need someone else to tell me if it's any good or worth playing, because I'm just biased replaying my own game haha!

comments.author: RecordingTechnical86
comments.body: I think it looks pretty cool. You need a unique selling point. Do you have that?

replies.author: Crignog
replies.body: Kind of? It's typical RTS rules, but everyone is a Human faction, in order to produce units of other races you have to capture their barracks/buildings around the map. It's Battlefield Conquest style play where you capture and hold locations to tick up points

replies.author: RecordingTechnical86
replies.body: Ah i see thats cool so kinda enslavement rts

replies.author: Crignog
replies.body: Hahaha, yeah exactly

comments.author: Hjalm
comments.body: I like the artstyle and the aethetics. If you're having fun and keep learning something it's never a waste of time imo.

replies.author: Crignog
replies.body: Appreciate that, yeah maybe being too hard on myself <3

comments.author: lemonlemons
comments.body: I like the style! Nothing is a waste of time, always learning something for next projects.

replies.author: Crignog
replies.body: When you're right you're right, thank you!

comments.author: newforest3d
comments.body: That looks great! Love the trees and the tilt shift

replies.author: Crignog
replies.body: Thank you! Video is quite low quality for this upload, but it's definitely more readable/clear in game haha

comments.author: Life-Heron-6533
comments.body: assets are from asset store right?

replies.author: Crignog
replies.body: Sprites are asset store bought that's right - 3D stuff like buildings and trees are generated

replies.author: Life-Heron-6533
replies.body: cool :D

comments.author: Kalaith
comments.body:
Ill be honest..  
I think it looks better then the recent rts releases  
I can at a glance tell the units apart, the spells/effects have noticable and impactful events

reminds me a little more of total war combat then a rts, might be worth looking into as a option

replies.author: Crignog
replies.body: Yeah I half went down this road with formations. You can hold right click to drag the formation position, but I didn't really go further with it. You might be right! But thanks for your kind words :)

comments.author: FrenchLiviela
comments.body:
Define a waste of time.

For you to play it yourself? Then no.

For someone else to play it? Perhaps. At some point everyone should be able to generate their own games of indie-caliber.

replies.author: Crignog
replies.body: Yeah, I don't necessarily plan on like, releasing it to steam. But for me to play and maybe some friends. Appreciate that insight <3

comments.author: blessed--
comments.body:
bro? u in your own head or something

the whole reason to make games is for fun, not to make a quick buck on steam

two completely different mindsets

if you're learning something then every project is worth, and it will take many projects to get to the successful game you want

just keep making things, release them, get 0 feedback or plays, and go again 

its like going to the gym

replies.author: Crignog
replies.body: Just wanna say thank you, I think I needed to hear this - absolutely making stuff for fun and not for money. Appreciate you man

comments.author: Toamy
comments.body:
I think it looks pretty appealing already. Not that I have tried myself but I think making it a well balanced RTS, like Age of empires etc. is probably something that will take a ton of work, so my suggestion would be to maybe to keep it simple and focus on the fun of building up an army and getting them into fights?

Where are you taking it direction wise?

replies.author: Crignog
replies.body: Yeah you are 100% right. I don't want to focus on the tiny details of balance and just want it to be fun. I explained in a comment above, but it's basically Battlefield Conquest as the primary mode, but captured points are production buildings for other races/monsters. So production of those units can only happen while holding those objectives

replies.author: Toamy
replies.body:
That sounds like a great concept imo!

As a kid I played a game called Seven Kingdoms and while I was way too young to understand half of what was going on, most of the fun I had playing was the bat shit crazy monsters you could get and see them stomp your opponent. I think game design wise if you lean into this risk / reward mechanic, where if you spread out your units to capture more points it naturally becomes harder to defend each individual point, but the reward should be huge if you succeed in that. Having some flashy big monster to run down your opponent with would be very cool.

Very interested in how you move forward!

replies.author: Crignog
replies.body: Hadn't heard of Seven Kingdoms before, but that looks sick. I especially like the idea of a Fort having a leader and a set maximum number of troops it can train. That might actually be something I look at including over typical population caps, as needing to build lots of houses to increase population ends up with just loads of houses at the end. You got it pretty much right though! Defending a shrine, shrines allow monster production, means big units that have activated abilities and much higher health

comments.author: darthbiki
comments.body:
I like the visuals and agree with the other comments - gamedev as a hobby is never a waste of time, as with any hobby.

Do you have a demo available yet?

replies.author: Crignog
replies.body: I'm pretty close to a demo I think, needs some models replacing, but there is a few campaign levels, single player skirmish and multiplayer modes as it stands. Appreciate that sentiment, thank you!

replies.author: darthbiki
replies.body: Cool, looking forward to the demo :)

replies.body: No the art is from here [Dreamir - itch.io](https://itch.io/profile/dreamir)

comments.author: M4xs0n
comments.body: Looks cool even tho I wouldn’t play it

comments.author: Makestroz
comments.body: if you're learning and enjoying yourself it's not a waste of time. this project might not be the one but that don't mean to stop. even completed games that aren't going to sell can be added to your portfolio to prove you have the ability to start and finish things, which is more important than it sounds.

replies.author: Crignog
replies.body: Yeah I think that's a huge point I need to ensure I remind myself of. If I can have it actually finished, like consider it done, I think that would be awesome. Thank you :)

comments.author: ScallionZestyclose16
comments.body:
Terrain looks a bit flat, I think it would do wonders with a more 3D based terrain like Warcraft 3 / Age of Empires.
Like add unpassable ravines, just to make the atmosphere a bit more grounded instead of just flat gamey arcade. :)

replies.author: Crignog
replies.body: Appreciate that observation! Yes, so at the moment I'm using Godot and TileMapLayer3D to build the "terrain". It allows for raise sections but it does mean map diversity isn't fantastic at the moment. I'll definitely have a look at this because I think the maps themselves will play a big role in whether it's fun or not as much as commanding an army

comments.author: mccoypauley
comments.body: Looks cute! I would play it
